intro: Juneteenth morning. US markets are closed — the first live session is Monday June 22. The macro environment has not improved during the holiday: DXY at 100.75 on Juneteenth FX (up from 100.15), VIX last printed at 17.0 (at the gate, not through it), and Bitcoin's two-day stop clock is executing with BTC at $62,520 at 11:03 UTC ($980 below the $63,500 stop). The single bright spot: SK Hynix extended to a third consecutive ATH at ₩2,764,000 (+2.94%) on the June 19 KOSPI, with HBM4E samples confirmed shipping — this is the portfolio's unconditional bull idea regardless of US macro regime. The ideas below are calibrated for the JUNE 22 open (first post-Juneteenth, post-FOMC full session). Three scenarios diverge from June 22: (A) VIX clears below 17 AND DXY breaks below 100 on the same session → conditional adds activate for NVDA; (B) DXY holds above 100 → NVDA add suspended, defensive posture extends; (C) SPX opens below 7,460 → full STEP_ASIDE triggered, reduce all longs. Watch BTC/IBIT flow data on June 22 for the first signal on post-stop re-entry timing.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: Third consecutive ATH at ₩2,764,000 — HBM4E samples confirmed; unconditional add on any pullback to ₩2,680,000–₩2,750,000.
ideas.why: SK Hynix has delivered three consecutive ATH closes on above-average volume with HBM4E sample shipments confirmed for June 2026 — approximately three weeks after Samsung's May 29 first shipment. TradingKey confirmed the shipments are 'as soon as this month,' initiating the customer qualification process that will determine 2027 mass-production allocation. The stock is ₩74,000 above the 38-analyst consensus average PT of ₩2,690,000, triggering a sell-side PT revision cycle toward ₩3.0M+. The KOSPI 9,000 milestone (first time in history) creates passive Korean ETF inflows as a structural bid. This is the portfolio's only unconditional BUY — US macro (VIX, DXY, FOMC) does not affect the KRX session timing or the HBM4E product calendar.
ideas.trigger: Any KOSPI session pullback to ₩2,680,000–₩2,750,000 (session-floor support zone from June 19) → add with stop raised to ₩2,540,000.
ideas.risk: Samsung announces credible HBM4E customer qualification win before SK Hynix completes its own process; or DXY sustained above 102 drives foreign selling that overwhelms domestic institutional buying over 3+ sessions.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: June 22 conditional add at $205–$215 ONLY if VIX <17 AND DXY <100 on same session — both gates required; Annual Meeting June 24 is the override catalyst.
ideas.why: NVDA closed June 18 at $208.82, the first close above the 50-DMA ($206.74) since the FOMC dump — the technical confirmation signal. But DXY has risen to 100.75 on Juneteenth FX trading (was 100.15 at June 18 close), making the June 22 gate-clear less probable than it appeared on June 18 evening. The framework requires VIX <17 AND DXY <100 on the same session before executing the $205–$215 add. If DXY holds above 100 on June 22, the add is suspended and the Annual Meeting June 24 becomes the next window — Jensen Huang's first post-FOMC public commentary on AI capex can override macro gates. The $25B bond raise (3.4x oversubscribed), SK Hynix three consecutive ATHs, and $91B Q2 revenue consensus confirm the fundamental thesis is intact.
ideas.trigger: June 22: VIX closes below 17 AND DXY closes below 100 → execute add at $205–$215, stop $195. If only one gate clears: do NOT add; wait for both. Annual Meeting June 24: if Jensen signals strong AI capex confidence → add regardless of gate status.
ideas.risk: DXY holds above 100 through June 22 (Fed hike pricing entrenched); VIX re-expands above 18 on a Warsh hawkish speech June 22–26; 30Y tests 5.00% — all three scenarios keep the conditional add suspended and extend the hold-without-adding period.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Stop execution expected — exit long position; no re-entry until two closes above $63,500 AND IBIT posts a daily inflow.
ideas.why: BTC at $62,520 at 11:03 UTC June 19 (Crypto.com MCP live) is $980 below the $63,500 two-day close stop on Day 2, with ~13 hours to UTC midnight close. Bitcoin spot ETF weekly outflows hit a RECORD $1.72B (Bitcoin Foundation); IBIT has posted 11 consecutive days of outflows; Fear & Greed Index collapsed to 8 (extreme fear). The framework is unambiguous: two consecutive UTC daily closes below $63,500 = STOP EXECUTES, EXIT FULL POSITION. The probability of a $980 recovery on thin Juneteenth holiday liquidity against an 11-day IBIT outflow streak is minimal. Strategy (MicroStrategy) is also selling BTC per Investing.com — dual institutional exit (ETF + corporate treasury) is a regime change, not a cyclical event.
ideas.trigger: Exit long position at current liquidity (stop already triggered on Day 1 June 18). Re-entry requires: (1) BTC produces TWO consecutive UTC daily closes ABOVE $63,500, AND (2) IBIT posts at least one daily inflow on those same sessions. Monitor farside.co.uk for daily ETF flow data.
ideas.risk: BTC miraculously recovers to $63,500+ by UTC midnight June 19 (low probability) — if the stop clock resets on Day 2 resolution, upgrade back to HOLD/watch and monitor for June 22 IBIT flow data. The re-entry discipline (two closes above + IBIT inflow) holds regardless.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Step aside — monitor June 22 opening price at $165–$175 for stabilization watch; do not chase and do not bottom-fish before two closes above $185.
ideas.why: The $185 daily close stop triggered at $174.90 on June 18 (-8.82%) — the framework is unambiguous: exit. US markets are closed today (Juneteenth). The June 22 open is the diagnostic: SPCX opening $165–$175 with recovering volume (>150M shares) initiates a 3–5 session stabilization watch. The June 20 weekly options expiry (tomorrow) clears the $195 gamma headwind and resets to July options at ~52–55% IV as the preferred hedge instrument for any re-entry. DXY at 100.75 (Juneteenth FX) is adverse for the highest-multiple name in the US market (84x revenue). The fundamental franchise (Starlink, Starship, Cursor AI, Starshield) is intact; the September 2 earnings is the next anchor event.
ideas.trigger: June 22: SPCX opens $165–$175 + volume >150M shares → begin stabilization watch (do not buy yet); two consecutive daily closes ABOVE $185 on above-average volume = re-entry signal with new stop at $165. If SPCX opens below $165 on June 22 → correction extending, wait for $150–$160 zone.
ideas.risk: Stop already triggered — the defined risk has been realized. Risk of re-entry: FOMC hawkish regime extends (DXY above 102) further compresses 84x multiple; September 2 earnings disappoints vs $2.4T implied expectations.

ideas.name: Meta Platforms
ideas.idea: Best post-FOMC dip buy in megacap tech — self-funded AI, -5.44% on June 17, entering a recovering macro tape.
ideas.why: Meta fell -5.44% on June 17 — worst FOMC-session move among megacaps. But Meta is the cleanest fundamental story in big tech: AI capex funded entirely from operations (no debt, no external dependency), strong revenue acceleration, and the cheapest forward multiple in the Magnificent-7 post-selloff. At ~$548, Meta is well below institutional target prices. If VIX normalizes below 17 on June 22, META is the highest-beta recovery trade in big tech — the stock with the most compressed FOMC premium and the cleanest fundamental picture. Self-funded AI means the Warsh rate path is structurally less relevant to META than to NVDA or SPCX.
ideas.trigger: June 22 open: VIX below 18 and recovering + META holds $545 support → buy at $545–$560 with stop at $530 daily close.
ideas.risk: 30Y Treasury tests 5.00% post-Juneteenth → multiple compression accelerates for long-duration growth across the board; META's ~25x P/E, while not extreme, is still vulnerable if the 30Y gate breaks.

ideas.name: SPDR Energy Select Sector ETF
ideas.idea: Iran ceasefire formally signed June 19 in Switzerland — oil supply increasing, H2 earnings estimate cuts not yet in sell-side numbers.
ideas.why: The Iran ceasefire formal signing ceremony in Switzerland on June 19 confirms Hormuz reopening on a 30-day timeline. Brent at $78 is structurally $9–12 below the $87–90 embedded in energy equity models. H2 2026 energy sector earnings estimate cuts of 8–12% are still not in sell-side consensus — that recognition event is the medium-term catalyst for XLE downside. Warsh's hawkish FOMC (risk-off + dollar strength) is an incremental tailwind for the XLE short: commodity equities underperform in high-DXY, risk-off environments. The sell-side note cycle (energy analysts revising H2 estimates downward) typically lags by 4–6 weeks from the oil catalyst — we are in the prime window.
ideas.trigger: Any Brent bounce to $82–$85 on mine-clearance timeline delays is the better short entry size-up moment. June 22 open is the next sizing decision — if XLE opens above $54, add to the short position.
ideas.risk: Iran deal collapses or Strait of Hormuz clearance delayed beyond 60 days; Brent closes above $90 on two consecutive sessions → cover all shorts immediately.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: Post-FOMC dip at $375–$390 — Azure AI monetization compounds regardless of rate path; least rate-sensitive megacap AI play.
ideas.why: Microsoft fell ~3.79% on June 17, creating the first meaningful pullback since the SPCX IPO narrative temporarily dominated headlines. At ~$378, Azure AI monetization and Copilot attach rates are compounding quietly. Microsoft's recurring enterprise revenue model (contracted, subscription-based) makes it the least DCF-sensitive to rate uncertainty among the megacaps — the cash flows are real, current, and growing, not projected far-future earnings. The post-FOMC entry window at $375–$390 with a clear stop at $368 is the cleanest risk-adjusted entry in megacap tech for the post-Juneteenth macro recovery scenario.
ideas.trigger: VIX begins recovering below 18 on June 22 AND MSFT holds $375 support → buy at $375–$390, stop $368 daily close.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-monetization lag extends (capex accelerating faster than Azure revenue); SPCX narrative continues pulling growth capital allocation away from 'mature AI' incumbents; rate environment deteriorates further (30Y above 5.00%).
